key_insight: Physis-Lang argues that natural language can serve as a physical representation for video world models if it is allowed to self-evolve with the model. This reframes language from a weak description tool into a core medium for capturing and updating physical knowledge.
problem_solved: The paper tackles the gap between visually realistic video prediction and physically consistent world modeling. It addresses the challenge that many video generators can produce plausible frames while still violating basic physical principles like motion, interaction, and object permanence.
method: Introduce Physis-Lang: a self-evolving language framework that encodes physical knowledge for video world modeling.
Iteratively update language-based physical representations as the model observes and predicts world dynamics.
Use language as the primary physical abstraction instead of relying only on extra visual, latent, numerical, or planning signals.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests a simpler and more interpretable way to improve physical consistency in video generation and world models. It may reduce dependence on specialized auxiliary representations while making model behavior easier to inspect and refine.

paper_title: Physis-Lang: Self-Evolving Language as a Physical Representation for Video World Model
paper_authors: Liming Lu, Xianzheng Ma, Wenkun He, Guanqi Zhan, Yilin Zhao
